<!-- head-1: body_md -->
The difference in potential energy density between the unstable perturbative vacuum \( (\phi = 0)\) and the stable non-perturbative minimum \((\phi = \phi_0)\) exactly equals the total spatial tension \(T_{p}\) of the underlying Dp-brane system
 \begin{equation}
 V(0)-V(\phi _{0})=T_{p}
 \end{equation}
 At the global minimum  the negative potential energy precisely cancels the mass-energy density of the brane.
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
While the global minimum represents a completely homogeneous vacuum, the classical string field equations  admit non-trivial, spatially dependent lump solutions (solitonic configurations). A lump solution \(\Psi_{\text{lump}}(x)\) that transitions asymptotically along a spatial direction \(x^i \to \infty\) to the stable minimum \(\phi_0\), but passes through the unstable maximum \(\phi=0\) at a localized codimensional interface, describes a stable lower-dimensional D(p-n)-brane, where \(n<p\).
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
At the global stable minimum \(\Psi _{\text{tv}}\), the original D-brane has entirely dissolved. Because open strings require the boundary conditions provided by a physical D-brane to exist, there are no physical open string physical degrees of freedom left in the spectrum around \(\Psi _{\text{tv}}\).
<!-- end head-3 -->
